content:
ryan: Heads up — saw a regression on nightly dedicated runs: sudden HBM bandwidth spike + KV eviction jitter during synth long-seq workload. Uploaded nsys slice.
perf-bot: nsys report: /artifacts/2790012345_ns_report.qdrep (summary attached)
marta: thanks — what changed in the kernel selector recently? any deploys to dedicated pools?
ryan: rolled kernel-selector patch `choose_by_cost_v2` on Tue. It prefers smaller-kernel fast-paths for predicted short seqs. We're seeing many seqs labeled short but actually run long (long tail). That mismap hits the KV path.
sadaf: quick take — if a long seq goes through a small-kernel path, KV cache misses explode because the implementation expects different KV page layout. That leads to lots of `kv_evict_slab` churn.
eng-runner: I pulled the nsys timeline: looks like bursts of `kv_read_page` followed by waves of `kv_evict_slab` and then `cudaMemcpyAsync` backfills. HBM BW graph shows sustained 420-480 GB/s in 200ms windows (baseline ~260).
ryan: paste from nsys summary:
```
nsys timeline summary:
  attention_forward_fp16        31.8%  avg 1.18ms  (kernel choice: large-attention)
  kv_read_page                  21.6%  avg 0.62ms  (frequent stalls waiting for HBM)
  kv_evict_slab                 12.4%  avg 0.42ms  (bursty)
  cudaMemcpyAsync               17.9%  avg 0.35ms  (host<>device noise)
  scheduler_idle                16.3%
HBM bandwidth peak: 492 GB/s
HBM sustained during waves: 430 GB/s
```
marta: interesting — scheduler_idle suggests batching heuristics still trying to pack requests but KV churn prevents kernel completion. Any correlation with microbatch sizes? ryan: yes — microbatch size is constant but token counts vary; dynamic-window-v2 batching groups by token count but uses a sampled prefix estimate that undercounts tail tokens.
sadaf: config snippet from canary:
```
runtime:
  kernel_selector:
    strategy: "latency_cost_v2"
  batching:
    strategy: "dynamic-window-v2"
    window_ms: 8
    sample_prefix: 32
  kv:
    prefetch: true
    prefetch_pages: 1
    eviction_policy: "lru"
```
ryan: hypothesis: sample_prefix=32 underestimates for many customer traces (we've got ~2% of requests with long tail >2k tokens). Those get routed to fast-path kernels that don't keep KV hot, leading to eviction oscillation and excessive HBM reads/writes.
perf-bot: regression delta since last good: +18% p99 latency, +35% HBM bandwidth usage on synth-longseq workload.
marta: can we repro with a focused harness? suggested steps: 1) synthetic run with sequence mixture (short/long skew 98/2), 2) run nsys + perfetto with kernel timestamps, 3) vary sample_prefix and window_ms.
eng-runner: I ran a quick local repro: toggling `kernel_selector` back to `choose_by_seqlen_v1` drops HBM BW down to ~260GB/s and evictions become rare. So selector is the trigger.
ryan: temporary mitigation: bump sample_prefix -> 256 and bump prefetch_pages -> 3. That reduced eviction wave amplitude in the local run.
sadaf: long-term: we should (a) add a quick microclassifier to detect tail-heavy requests before kernel selection, (b) modify kernel-selector to prefer KV-friendly kernel for requests with even moderate tail risk, (c) assert better telemetry for per-request predicted_vs_actual_seqlen.
marta: also add a perfetto hook to capture L2/HBM DMA counters during tail windows — that'll help isolate whether stalls are DMA or compute-bound.
ryan: logs I grabbed from the failing run (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] request id=abc123 predicted_len=48 actual_len=2304 kernel_chosen=fast_att_fp16 kv_prefetch=false
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] kernel attention_forward_fp16 start=0.12ms end=1.30ms
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] kv_read_page start=1.31ms stall=0.58ms hbm_wait=true
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] kv_evict_slab triggered pages=8
```
eng-runner: propose short runbook: revert selector on canary, add sample_prefix AB test, run 10k synthetic long-tail requests, capture nsys+perfetto, and escalate if p99 > baseline+10%.
ryan: I'll open a PR for the revert + sample_prefix AB and kick off a canary run. tagging @marta @sadaf for review. Thanks.
marta: ack. let's also add a unit microbench for `kv_evict_slab` so we can baseline eviction cost across kernels.
sadaf: adding notes to the perf checklist: instrument per-request `predicted_len` vs `actual_len` and a new metric `kv_pressure_score` (0-100).
perf-bot: task created: PERF-4281 (investigate kernel-selector long-tail regression) — perf artifacts attached.
ryan: will post the canary nsys links once the run finishes. small followup: consider a short-term rule to prefer KV-friendly kernels when `prefetch_pages>1` to avoid mixing strategies.
marta: agreed. short-term rule + telemetry + AB test. good triage.
